name: Abdullah Taha Bakhsh

summary.text: Abdullah Taha Bakhsh is a Saudi investor who, through Traco International N.V., a Netherlands Antilles company he wholly owns, and other companies he controls, held more than five percent of Harken Energy's common stock for more than ten consecutive years until 1999, according to Harken's SEC filings. Press accounts say he joined Harken as a major investor in 1987 as part of a financing arranged by Jackson Stephens with Union Bank of Switzerland, and was represented on Harken's board by Talat Othman.

facts.claim: A 2001 Schedule 13D/A filed with the SEC describes Traco International as a Netherlands Antilles corporation one hundred percent owned and controlled by Abdullah Taha Bakhsh, a citizen of Saudi Arabia, who used his personal funds to capitalise it.
facts.quote: Traco is a Netherlands Antilles corporation which is one hundred percent owned and controlled by Abdullah Taha Bakhsh ("Mr. Bakhsh"), a citizen of Saudi Arabia.

sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Harken Energy Corp. Schedule 13D/A)
sources.title: Harken Energy Corp — Schedule 13D/A (Traco International N.V.)

facts.claim: The same filing states that through Traco and other foreign corporations he owned, controlled and capitalised, Bakhsh indirectly held more than five percent of Harken's common stock for more than ten consecutive years until 1999, when equity transactions took him below the threshold.
facts.quote: Mr. Bakhsh indirectly held and owned over five percent of the Issuer's Common Stock for more than ten consecutive years until 1999.

sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Harken Energy Corp. Schedule 13D/A)
sources.title: Harken Energy Corp — Schedule 13D/A (Traco International N.V.)

facts.claim: On 3 July 2001 Bakhsh, through Traco, bought 98,500 Harken shares in the open market for $233,260, taking his indirect holding back above five percent.
facts.quote: On July 3, 2001, indirectly through Traco, Mr. Bakhsh purchased 98,500 shares of the Issuer's Common Stock in the open market for aggregate consideration of $233,260.00

facts.quote: Traco is wholly-owned by Mr. Bakhsh, and Atherstone is indirectly owned by Mr. Bakhsh

facts.claim: The Texas Observer in 1991 listed Bakhsh as owner of Traco International and Atherstone International, major shareholders in Harken, represented on Harken's board by Talat Othman.
facts.quote: owner of Traco International and Atherstone International, major shareholders in Harken; represented on Harken's board by Talat Othman

facts.claim: Press chronologies state that in 1987 Arkansas investment banker Jackson Stephens arranged $25 million in financing for Harken from Union Bank of Switzerland in return for a stock interest, and that Bakhsh joined Harken's board as a major investor as part of that deal.
facts.quote: In 1987, Stephens made arrangements with Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) to provide $25 million to Harken in return for a stock interest in Harken.

connections.quote: Mr. Bakhsh indirectly held and owned over five percent of the Issuer's Common Stock for more than ten consecutive years until 1999.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: Bakhsh as a 'BCCI financier'. No primary source links Bakhsh to BCCI; a 2004 opinion piece by Lucy Komisar says his chief banker was BCCI shareholder Khalid bin Mahfouz, and a partisan chronology says Stephens, UBS and Bakhsh each had ties to BCCI. These are secondary and partisan; the Senate BCCI report's text on Harken or Bakhsh was not located. Recorded as unsupported pending a primary source.
Site claim tested: that Harken 'secured offshore Bahrain drilling rights and capital from BCCI-connected financiers'. The Bahrain concession was not researched here.
The often-cited 17 percent figure for Bakhsh's stake was not found in any source; the SEC filings say 'over five percent'.
Talat Othman's board seat rests on the Texas Observer; Harken proxy statements would confirm it.
